def-csm-finite-range-lattice-interaction: Fix an integer dimension $d\geq1$ and a finite nonempty alphabet $A$. A configuration is a function $\sigma:\mathbb Z^d\to A$. An interaction list consists of a finite index set $\mathcal R$ and, for each $r\in\mathcal R$, a finite nonempty shape $S_r\subset\mathbb Z^d$ containing $0$ and a function $\Phi_r:A^{S_r}\to\mathbb R$. The index $r$ is part of the data: two equal shapes with different indices represent two terms and are both counted. Every translate $x+S_r$ contributes once, with value $\Phi_r((\sigma_{x+y})_{y\in S_r})$.

The range is $R=\max_{r\in\mathcal R}\operatorname{diam}_\infty(S_r)$, with $R=0$ when $\mathcal R$ is empty. For finite $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d$, define the free-volume energy and the energy conditioned on an exterior configuration $\eta\in A^{\Lambda^c}$ by
$$H^{\mathrm{free}}_\Lambda(\sigma)=\sum_{r\in\mathcal R}\ \sum_{x:x+S_r\subseteq\Lambda}\Phi_r(\sigma_{x+S_r}),\qquad E_\Lambda(\tau_\Lambda\mid\eta)=\sum_{r\in\mathcal R}\ \sum_{x:(x+S_r)\cap\Lambda\ne\varnothing}\Phi_r((\tau_\Lambda\eta)_{x+S_r}).$$
These are finite sums: for each finite shape $S_r$, only finitely many anchors $x$ make $x+S_r$ meet $\Lambda$. Terms meeting $\Lambda$ but not contained in it appear in the conditional energy and not in the free-volume energy. The definitions are mathematical and assign no physical units; a physical model must state its units separately.
def-csm-lattice-gibbs-specification: Assume Countable Choice for the product-measure extension framework of [[def-countable-choice]] and [[lem-csm-lattice-product-and-measure-compactness]]. Work in the finite-alphabet configuration space $X=A^{\mathbb Z^d}$ with its cylinder-generated Borel sigma-algebra. Let the finite-range interaction and its conditional energy be as in [[def-csm-finite-range-lattice-interaction]], and fix $\beta>0$. For a finite $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d$ and exterior configuration $\eta\in A^{\Lambda^c}$, put
$$Z_\Lambda^\eta=\sum_{\tau\in A^\Lambda}e^{-\beta E_\Lambda(\tau\mid\eta)},\qquad \gamma_\Lambda(f\mid\eta)=\frac{\sum_{\tau\in A^\Lambda}f(\tau\eta)e^{-\beta E_\Lambda(\tau\mid\eta)}}{Z_\Lambda^\eta}$$
for bounded measurable $f:X\to\mathbb R$. Here $\gamma_\Lambda f$ denotes the function $\eta\mapsto\gamma_\Lambda(f\mid\eta)$, composition is operator composition, and $\mu\gamma_\Lambda(f)=\int\gamma_\Lambda(f\mid\eta)\,d\mu(\eta)$. A proper kernel leaves every exterior-measurable event fixed. A specification is a family $(\gamma_\Lambda)_{\Lambda\text{ finite}}$ of proper probability kernels satisfying $\gamma_\Lambda\gamma_\Delta=\gamma_\Lambda$ whenever $\Delta\subseteq\Lambda$. A DLR state is a probability measure $\mu$ on $X$ satisfying $\mu\gamma_\Lambda=\mu$ for every finite $\Lambda$.

For the existence and uniqueness results below, a specification has **finite range** when for every finite $\Delta$ and every cylinder event $C$ the function $\eta\mapsto\gamma_\Delta(\mathbf1_C\mid\eta)$ depends on only finitely many coordinates of $\eta$. The displayed finite-range Gibbs formula has this property because only finitely many interaction terms meet $\Delta$, and a cylinder indicator depends on only finitely many additional coordinates.

The formula is the candidate Gibbs specification; [[lem-csm-lattice-specification-consistency]] establishes its positive finite normalization, measurability, properness and consistency under the stated hypotheses. The Countable Choice assumption is used for the product-measure construction, not for any finite conditional sum.
lem-csm-lattice-product-and-measure-compactness: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $d\geq1$, let $A$ be a finite nonempty set, and put $X=A^{\mathbb Z^d}$. Give $X$ the metric $d_X(\sigma,\eta)=\sum_{n\geq1}2^{-n}\mathbf 1_{\{\sigma_{i_n}\ne\eta_{i_n}\}}$ for a fixed enumeration $(i_n)$ of $\mathbb Z^d$, and let $\mathcal C$ be its cylinder algebra. Then $X$ is compact, the Borel sigma-algebra is $\sigma(\mathcal C)$, and every consistent normalized finitely additive probability on $\mathcal C$ extends uniquely to a probability on $\sigma(\mathcal C)$. Moreover, every sequence of probabilities on this sigma-algebra has a subsequence whose cylinder probabilities converge to those of a probability measure; along that subsequence integrals of every continuous $f:X\to\mathbb R$ converge.
lem-csm-lattice-specification-consistency: Assume the finite-alphabet product-measure convention and conditional Gibbs formula of [[def-csm-lattice-gibbs-specification]], a finite-range interaction, and $\beta>0$. For every finite $\Lambda$ and exterior $\eta$, the displayed partition $Z_\Lambda^\eta$ is finite and strictly positive, the formula $\gamma_\Lambda(\cdot\mid\eta)$ defines a measurable proper probability kernel, and the family satisfies $\gamma_\Lambda\gamma_\Delta=\gamma_\Lambda$ whenever finite $\Delta\subseteq\Lambda$.
thm-csm-chain-dlr-uniqueness: Assume Countable Choice, finite $\beta>0$, finite $J,h\in\mathbb R$, and the one-dimensional nearest-neighbor Ising specification from [[def-csm-lattice-gibbs-specification]]. Then there is exactly one DLR state. It is the stationary Markov law constructed from the positive transfer matrix in [[lem-csm-chain-markov-bridge]]. For every fixed cylinder, finite-interval Gibbs probabilities converge to that law uniformly over the two endpoint boundary spins.
thm-csm-ising-coexistence-pressure-cusp: Assume Countable Choice. For the two-dimensional nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic Ising model with $J>0$, $h=0$, and $\beta J\geq2$, the dimensionless pressure per site $p(h)$ as a function of field $h$ is not differentiable at $h=0$. More precisely, if the stationary DLR states at zero field have magnetizations at least $m_*>0$ and at most $-m_*$, then every positive-field secant slope from zero is at least $\beta m_*$ and every negative-field secant slope is at most $-\beta m_*$. This proves a sufficient coexistence cusp; it does not identify the critical coupling.
thm-csm-ising-high-temperature-state: Assume Countable Choice, spins $s_i\in\{-1,+1\}$, inverse temperature $\beta>0$, a constant finite field $h\in\mathbb R$, and symmetric pair couplings satisfying $J_{ij}=J_{ji}$, $J_{i+k,j+k}=J_{ij}$ for all $i,j,k\in\mathbb Z^d$, and $J_{ij}=0$ when $\|i-j\|_\infty>R$ for some finite $R$. For finite $\Lambda$, use the conditional energy
$$E_\Lambda(s_\Lambda\mid\eta)=-\sum_{\{i,j\}:\{i,j\}\cap\Lambda\ne\varnothing}J_{ij}\widehat s_i\widehat s_j-h\sum_{i\in\Lambda}s_i,$$
where $\widehat s_i=s_i$ on $\Lambda$ and $\widehat s_i=\eta_i$ outside; let $\gamma$ be the corresponding finite-alphabet Gibbs specification from [[def-csm-lattice-gibbs-specification]]. If
$$\sup_i\sum_j\tanh(\beta|J_{ij}|)<1,$$
then there exists exactly one DLR state. For homogeneous nearest-neighbor coupling $J$ this sufficient condition is $2d\tanh(\beta|J|)<1$. It is not asserted to be sharp.
thm-csm-ising-low-temperature-coexistence: Assume Countable Choice. For the nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic Ising model on $\mathbb Z^2$ with coupling $J>0$, zero field, and $\beta J\geq2$, there exist two distinct translation-stationary DLR states $\mu_+$ and $\mu_-$ such that for every site $i$,
$$\mu_+(s_i)\geq m_*>0,\qquad \mu_-(s_i)\leq-m_*.$$
One may take $m_*=1-2\delta(\beta J)$, where
$$\delta(K)=\frac43\,\frac{r^4(5-4r)}{(1-r)^2},\qquad r=3e^{-2K}.$$
This is a sufficient low-temperature bound; the states are not asserted to be extremal and $K=2$ is not claimed to be critical.
thm-csm-lattice-van-hove-pressure: Let $d\geq1$, $A$ be finite nonempty, and let a bounded translation-invariant finite-range interaction on $A^{\mathbb Z^d}$ be as in [[def-csm-finite-range-lattice-interaction]]. Fix $\beta>0$. For a van Hove sequence of finite sets $\Lambda_n\subset\mathbb Z^d$, meaning $|\Lambda_n|\to\infty$ and $|\{x\in\Lambda_n:\operatorname{dist}_\infty(x,\Lambda_n^c)\leq r\}|/|\Lambda_n|\to0$ for every fixed $r$, the free-boundary pressure
$$p_{\Lambda_n}=\frac{1}{|\Lambda_n|}\log\sum_{\sigma\in A^{\Lambda_n}}e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda_n}^{\rm free}(\sigma)}$$
converges to the same finite limit as along cubic boxes. Bounded finite-range interactions are essential; this statement does not concern continuum particles or long-range models.

lem-qsm-finite-matrix-cstar-and-state-duality: Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, $D=\dim H\ge1$, with inner product linear in its first argument. With composition, Hilbert adjoint, identity and the induced operator norm, $\mathcal B(H)$ is a nonzero unital complex C*-algebra in the sense of [[def-c-star-algebra]]. In particular it is complete, $\|AB\|\le\|A\|\|B\|$, $\|A^*A\|=\|A\|^2$, $\|A^*\|=\|A\|$ and $\|I\|=1$. The matrix $\|A\|^2I-A^*A$ is positive semidefinite and has a positive square root in $\mathcal B(H)$.

Every complex-linear functional $\omega:\mathcal B(H)\to\mathbb C$ that is positive, meaning $\omega(B^*B)\ge0$ for all $B$, has a unique positive semidefinite matrix $\rho$ such that $\omega(A)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A)$ for all $A$. It is bounded and satisfies

$$|\omega(A)|\le\operatorname{Tr}(\rho)\|A\|\quad(A\in\mathcal B(H)),\qquad \|\omega\|=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho)=\omega(I).$$

Consequently the canonical states of [[def-state-on-a-c-star-algebra]] are exactly the trace pairings of density operators of [[def-qc-density-operator]]; for a positive functional, normalization $\omega(I)=1$ is equivalent to norm one. The result includes zero positive functionals, nonfaithful densities and $D=1$; it makes no infinite-dimensional density representation assertion.
lem-qsm-matrix-state-calculus: Let $H$ be a complex inner-product space of finite dimension $D\geq1$, with inner product linear in its first argument. Every Hermitian endomorphism $M$ has an orthonormal eigenbasis with real eigenvalues. For a real function $f$ on its finite spectrum, define $f(M)$ by its spectral projections; this definition is independent of the choice of eigenbasis. In particular positive square roots, exponentials, and logarithms on positive supports are well defined.

For a density matrix $\rho$ on $H$, meaning a Hermitian positive semidefinite operator with $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$, $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A)=\sum_jp_j\langle Au_j,u_j\rangle$ for bounded $A$, where $\rho=\sum_jp_j|u_j\rangle\langle u_j|$. The weighted form $(X,Y)_\rho=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho X^*Y)$ satisfies Cauchy–Schwarz, $|(X,Y)_\rho|^2\leq(X,X)_\rho(Y,Y)_\rho$. Finally, $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho^2)\leq1$, with equality exactly for rank-one densities, and those are exactly the extreme points of the finite density-matrix set.

def-qsm-local-spin-algebras: Fix an integer dimension $d\ge1$, the countable site set $\Gamma=\mathbb{Z}^d$ of [[lem-qsm-integer-lattice-countable]], and one finite spin dimension $q\ge1$. Equip $\Gamma$ with the max-coordinate metric $d_\infty(x,y)=\max_{1\le r\le d}|x_r-y_r|$; symmetry and separation hold coordinatewise, and the triangle inequality follows from $|x_r-z_r|\le|x_r-y_r|+|y_r-z_r|$ for every coordinate. A **finite region** is a finite subset $\Lambda\subseteq\Gamma$; its cardinality is $|\Lambda|$.

For a finite region $\Lambda$, let $S_\Lambda=\{1,\ldots,q\}^{\Lambda}$ be the set of spin configurations on $\Lambda$ and let $\mathcal H_\Lambda$ be the vector space of functions $f:S_\Lambda\to\mathbb C$ with inner product $\langle f,g\rangle=\sum_{s\in S_\Lambda}f(s)\overline{g(s)}$. For each $s\in S_\Lambda$, let $e_s$ be the indicator function of $\{s\}$; these vectors form an orthonormal basis. For $\Lambda=\varnothing$, $S_\Lambda$ is a singleton and $\mathcal H_\Lambda\cong\mathbb C$. The **local spin matrix algebra** is

$$\mathcal A_\Lambda:=\mathcal B(\mathcal H_\Lambda)\cong M_{q^{|\Lambda|}}(\mathbb C),$$

Here $\mathcal B(\mathcal H_\Lambda)$ denotes all complex-linear endomorphisms of the finite-dimensional Hilbert space; they are bounded. The algebra has composition, Hilbert adjoint, identity $I_\Lambda$, and induced operator norm

$$\|T\|:=\sup_{\|\xi\|=1}\|T\xi\|.$$

The **finite local trace** is $\operatorname{Tr}_\Lambda(T):=\sum_{s\in S_\Lambda}\langle T e_s,e_s\rangle$ in the displayed configuration basis $(e_s)$. This is the usual finite-matrix trace; basis independence and its cyclic/unitary identities are supplied by [[lem-qsm-matrix-state-calculus]].

If $\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda'$, restriction of configurations gives the canonical factorization $\mathcal H_{\Lambda'}\cong\mathcal H_\Lambda\otimes\mathcal H_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}$, with sites ordered lexicographically. The **factor inclusion** is the unital $*$-homomorphism $\iota_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}:\mathcal A_\Lambda\to\mathcal A_{\Lambda'}$ given by $T\mapsto T\otimes I_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}$. A **localization region** for $T$ is any finite $\Lambda$ for which $T\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$ under these inclusions; a localization region need not be minimal.

The ordinary operator norm makes each local matrix algebra a nonzero unital complete C*-algebra, and every positive normalized complex-linear functional is uniquely a trace pairing with a density matrix, by [[lem-qsm-finite-matrix-cstar-and-state-duality]]. This includes the empty region, whose Hilbert space is $\mathbb C$. This definition does not posit an infinite-dimensional tensor-product Hilbert space.
def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra: Use the finite local matrix algebras and isometric factor inclusions of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]] and [[lem-qsm-local-spin-inclusions-isometric]]. Identify $A\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$ with its image in every larger finite-region algebra. The directed union

$$\mathcal A_{\mathrm{loc}}:=\bigcup_{\Lambda\subseteq\Gamma,\ |\Lambda|<\infty}\mathcal A_\Lambda$$

is the algebra of **strictly local observables**. Its norm is $\|A\|=\|A\|_{\mathcal A_\Lambda}$ for any finite localization region $\Lambda$ of $A$; isometric inclusions make this independent of the chosen region. The **quasi-local spin algebra** is the norm completion

$$\mathcal A:=\overline{\mathcal A_{\mathrm{loc}}}^{\,\|\cdot\|}.$$

The C*-algebra structure on this completion has product and adjoint extended continuously from the finite local matrix algebras. Countable Choice is assumed for the published existence theorem for metric completions; [[lem-qsm-quasilocal-completion]] supplies the full extension argument using the finite C*-identity of [[lem-qsm-finite-matrix-cstar-and-state-duality]].

**No global Hilbert tensor product is selected.** “Quasi-local” means norm completion of the directed algebra of finite-region observables; it does not mean a chosen representation as operators on an infinite tensor-product Hilbert space. A local operator $A\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$ may have more than one localization region. Disjoint finite local factors commute in their common finite tensor algebra.
lem-qsm-quasilocal-completion: Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the Cauchy-sequence completion. For the local spin system of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]], the normed $*$-algebra $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{loc}}$ and its completion $\mathcal A$ of [[def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra]] are well defined; $\mathcal A$ is a unital complex C*-algebra and $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{loc}}$ is norm dense in it. If $A\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$ and $B\in\mathcal A_\Delta$ for disjoint finite regions $\Lambda,\Delta$, then $AB=BA$.

def-qsm-bounded-finite-range-interaction: Use the lattice $\Gamma=\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge1$, the finite spin dimension $q\ge1$, the local matrix algebras $\mathcal A_\Lambda$, and the max-coordinate metric $d_\infty$ of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]]. For finite nonempty $Z\subset\Gamma$, write $\operatorname{diam}_\infty Z=\max_{x,y\in Z}d_\infty(x,y)$; for finite nonempty $X,Y\subset\Gamma$, write $\operatorname{dist}_\infty(X,Y)=\min_{x\in X,y\in Y}d_\infty(x,y)$.

A **uniformly bounded finite-range interaction** is a family $\Phi(Z)\in\mathcal A_Z$, indexed by finite nonempty $Z\subset\Gamma$, such that $\Phi(Z)^*=\Phi(Z)$ and there are an integer $M\ge1$, a finite $R\ge0$, and $\kappa<\infty$ satisfying

$$\Phi(Z)=0\quad\text{if }|Z|>M\text{ or }\operatorname{diam}_\infty Z>R,\qquad\kappa:=\sup_{x\in\Gamma}\sum_{Z\ni x}\|\Phi(Z)\|<\infty.$$

The norm in this sum is the operator norm in the local matrix algebra $\mathcal A_Z$. If a model lists several terms with the same support, first add them in that local algebra; the resulting single operator is $\Phi(Z)$, and $\kappa$ uses its norm. Thus no multiplicity is implicit.

For a finite region $\Lambda\subset\Gamma$, define the **free-boundary finite-volume Hamiltonian** by summing only terms whose complete support lies inside $\Lambda$; terms meeting $\Lambda$ but extending outside it are omitted:

$$H_\Lambda:=\sum_{\varnothing\ne Z\subseteq\Lambda}\Phi(Z)\in\mathcal A_\Lambda.$$

It is a finite sum of self-adjoint matrices. For a fixed scale $\hbar>0$ and any finite $\Omega\supseteq\Lambda$, embed $H_\Lambda$ in $\mathcal A_\Omega$ by the canonical factor inclusion and define

$$\alpha_t^\Lambda(A):=e^{itH_\Lambda/\hbar}Ae^{-itH_\Lambda/\hbar}\qquad(A\in\mathcal A_\Omega,\ t\in\mathbb R).$$

These actions are compatible as $\Omega$ increases, because the extra tensor factors carry the identity. On $\mathcal A_\Lambda$ this is the ordinary finite matrix Heisenberg dynamics.

In physical SI bookkeeping, when $\Phi(Z)$ is interpreted as an energy, $\Phi(Z)$, $\kappa$, and $H_\Lambda$ have units J, $t$ has units s, and $\hbar$ is the adopted reduced Planck constant with units J s. The mathematics below uses only $\hbar>0$ and asserts no measured parameter value.
thm-qsm-finite-range-spin-dynamics: Assume Countable Choice and the finite-matrix C*-identity condition [A1] below. Let $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{loc}}=\bigcup_{\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d,\ |\Lambda|<\infty}\mathcal A_\Lambda$ and let $\mathcal A$ be its norm completion as in [[def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra]]. These assumptions give the conditional unital C*-algebra structure supplied by [[lem-qsm-quasilocal-completion]]. Let $\Phi$ be a uniformly bounded finite-range interaction of [[def-qsm-bounded-finite-range-interaction]].

For any increasing finite exhaustion $\Lambda_n\uparrow\mathbb Z^d$, the free-boundary finite-volume maps $\alpha_t^{\Lambda_n}$ converge in norm on every local observable, uniformly for $t$ in compact intervals. Their limit is independent of the exhaustion and extends uniquely to a strongly continuous one-parameter group $\alpha_t$ of $*$-automorphisms of $\mathcal A$. Strong continuity means $t\mapsto\alpha_t(A)$ is norm-continuous for every fixed $A\in\mathcal A$. This result does not assert that an infinite-volume Hamiltonian is an element of $\mathcal A$ or a bounded operator on a preselected infinite tensor-product Hilbert space.

def-qsm-translation-invariant-spin-interaction: Use the lattice $\Gamma=\mathbb Z^d$, the finite-site Hilbert spaces, local matrix algebras, factor inclusions, and norm-completed local algebra $\mathcal A$ of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]] and [[def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra]]. Write $\tau_x$ for spatial translation by $x\in\Gamma$. For a finite region $\Lambda$ and its configuration basis $(e_s)_{s\in\{1,\ldots,q\}^{\Lambda}}$, the bijection $s\mapsto s_x$ defined by $s_x(y+x)=s(y)$ gives a unitary $U_{x,\Lambda}:\mathcal H_\Lambda\to\mathcal H_{\Lambda+x}$ by $U_{x,\Lambda}e_s=e_{s_x}$. On $A\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$ put $\tau_x(A)=U_{x,\Lambda}AU_{x,\Lambda}^*$.

For $x,y\in\Gamma$, the basis relabellings satisfy $U_{x,\Lambda+y}U_{y,\Lambda}=U_{x+y,\Lambda}$, since both sides send each configuration vector $e_s$ to $e_{s_{x+y}}$. Consequently $\tau_0$ is the identity and $\tau_{x+y}=\tau_x\circ\tau_y$ on local observables; continuity extends the action law to $\mathcal A$.

This local map is independent of the chosen localization region: enlarging $\Lambda$ tensors both representatives with identities, and the same site relabelling gives the corresponding enlarged unitary. On each finite region it is a unitary conjugation, hence isometric and preserves products, adjoints, and identities. It therefore extends uniquely to an isometric *-automorphism of the norm completion $\mathcal A$: if $A_n$ is local and converges to $A$, define $\tau_x(A)=\lim_n\tau_x(A_n)$; isometry makes this limit independent of the approximating sequence, and $\tau_{-x}$ is its inverse. This construction uses the norm-completion property and the isometric local maps; it does not use the separate finite-matrix C*-identity condition.

Let $\Phi$ be a uniformly bounded finite-range interaction in the sense of [[def-qsm-bounded-finite-range-interaction]], with parameters $M,R,\kappa$. It is translation invariant when $\tau_x(\Phi(Z))=\Phi(Z+x)$ for every finite nonempty support $Z$ and every $x\in\Gamma$. Let $\mathscr S_\Phi$ contain one representative of each nonzero translation orbit, anchored so that the lexicographically least site of each representative is $0$, using the standard coordinate lexicographic order on $\mathbb Z^d$. The least site exists because each support is finite and nonempty; every representative contains $0$. The list $\mathscr S_\Phi$ is finite: every such support has at most $M$ sites and lies in the finite cube $[-\lceil R\rceil,\lceil R\rceil]^d$. For finite $\Lambda$, the free-boundary Hamiltonian is $H_\Lambda=\sum_{Z\subseteq\Lambda}\Phi(Z)$, as in the interaction definition.

When $\Phi(Z)$ represents an energy, its norm, $H_\Lambda$, and the constant $J_\Phi:=\sum_{S\in\mathscr S_\Phi}\|\Phi(S)\|$ have units joules. The definition is mathematical and makes no empirical identification of an interaction with a material.

def-qsm-kms-state: Here a complex C$^*$-algebra is a complex Banach algebra with associative bilinear multiplication, submultiplicative norm, and a conjugate-linear involution satisfying $\|A^*A\|=\|A\|^2$; **unital** means that it has a nonzero identity $I$ ([[def-c-star-algebra]]). A $*$-automorphism is a bijective complex-linear map preserving multiplication and involution. Let $t\mapsto\alpha_t$ be a one-parameter group of such automorphisms, so $\alpha_0$ is the identity and $\alpha_s\alpha_t=\alpha_{s+t}$. It is **strongly continuous** when $t\mapsto\alpha_t(A)$ is norm-continuous for each fixed $A\in\mathcal A$. A **state** is a bounded complex-linear functional $\omega:\mathcal A\to\mathbb C$ with $\omega(I)=1$ and $\omega(A^*A)\ge0$ for every $A\in\mathcal A$; this is the state convention of [[def-qsm-infinite-algebraic-state]].

Fix absolute temperature $T>0$ in kelvins and Boltzmann's constant $k_B>0$ in J K$^{-1}$; the inverse-temperature parameter is $\beta:=(k_BT)^{-1}>0$, measured in J$^{-1}$. Let the reduced Planck constant $\hbar>0$ have units J s. Write $b:=\beta\hbar$, measured in seconds, and

$$S_b:=\{z\in\mathbb C:0\le\operatorname{Im}z\le b\},\qquad S_b^\circ:=\{z\in\mathbb C:0<\operatorname{Im}z<b\}.$$

A state $\omega$ is a **$\beta$-KMS state for $\alpha$ in physical time** when for every $A,B\in\mathcal A$ there is a bounded function $F_{A,B}:S_b\to\mathbb C$ (that is, $\sup_{z\in S_b}|F_{A,B}(z)|<\infty$) that is continuous on $S_b$, complex-differentiable at every point of $S_b^\circ$, and satisfies

$$F_{A,B}(t)=\omega\!\left(A\alpha_t(B)\right),\qquad F_{A,B}(t+ib)=\omega\!\left(\alpha_t(B)A\right)\quad(t\in\mathbb R).$$

For the assigned quantum spin model, $\mathcal A$ is the norm-completed quasi-local algebra of [[def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra]] and $\alpha$ is the thermodynamic dynamics of [[thm-qsm-finite-range-spin-dynamics]], under that theorem's stated hypotheses. The strip width is $\beta\hbar$ in physical seconds; setting $\hbar=1$ is a separate natural-unit convention. This is a mathematical equilibrium criterion for the specified algebra and dynamics. It does not assert that a model describes a material, that a system has dynamically relaxed, or that all stationary states are KMS.
lem-qsm-kms-strip-uniqueness: Let $b>0$ and $S_b=\{z\in\mathbb C:0\le\operatorname{Im}z\le b\}$, with interior $S_b^\circ=\{z:0<\operatorname{Im}z<b\}$. Let $F:S_b\to\mathbb C$ be bounded (so $\sup_{z\in S_b}|F(z)|<\infty$), continuous, and complex-differentiable at every point of $S_b^\circ$, and set

$$M_0:=\sup_{t\in\mathbb R}|F(t)|,\qquad M_1:=\sup_{t\in\mathbb R}|F(t+ib)|.$$

For $0<s<b$,

$$\sup_{t\in\mathbb R}|F(t+is)|\le M_0^{1-s/b}M_1^{s/b},$$

where each exponent is positive and $0^r=0$ for $r>0$. In particular, if $M_0,M_1\le C$ then $|F(z)|\le C$ on $S_b$. If two bounded continuous functions on $S_b$, holomorphic inside, have the same lower boundary values, then they agree on all of $S_b$.
thm-qsm-finite-kms-gibbs-characterization: Let $\mathcal H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space, let $H=H^*$ on $\mathcal H$ with energy units J, let $\hbar>0$ have units J s, and let $\beta>0$ have units J$^{-1}$. Write $\operatorname{Tr}$ for the ordinary finite-dimensional trace. Assume the finite spectral-calculus and unital C$^*$-algebra clauses [A1]–[A2] below. Define the finite-matrix Heisenberg group

$$\alpha_t^H(X):=e^{itH/\hbar}Xe^{-itH/\hbar}\qquad(X\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H),\ t\in\mathbb R).$$

A state $\omega$ on the unital C$^*$-algebra $\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ satisfies the $\beta$-KMS strip condition of [[def-qsm-kms-state]] for $\alpha^H$ if and only if

$$\omega(X)=\frac{\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H}X)}{\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H})}\qquad(X\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)).$$

Here $\beta$ has units J$^{-1}$, $H$ has units J, and the physical-time strip has width $\beta\hbar$ seconds. The result is finite-dimensional and makes no infinite-volume or relaxation claim.

item_dependency_levels.statement:
For the model of [[def-qsm-diagonal-ising-interaction]] and every finite $\Delta\subset\mathbb Z^d$, the displayed $\gamma_\Delta$ is a finite-range proper probability kernel, and the family $(\gamma_\Delta)_{\Delta\text{ finite}}$ satisfies $\gamma_\Lambda\gamma_\Delta=\gamma_\Lambda$ whenever $\Delta\subseteq\Lambda$. Thus it is a specification in the sense of [[def-csm-lattice-gibbs-specification]], including when the bounded finite-range coefficients depend on position.

If in addition $J_{i,i+v}=J(v)=J(-v)$ is translation invariant and $h_i=h$ is constant, this specification is exactly the CSM specification obtained by taking one interaction shape $\{0\}$ for the field and one shape $\{0,v\}$ for each chosen representative $v$ of the nonzero displacement pairs $\{v,-v\}$. The latter identification uses the translated-shape convention of [[def-csm-finite-range-lattice-interaction]] and agrees with [[lem-csm-lattice-specification-consistency]].

Assume Countable Choice and the finite-matrix C*-identity for the local spin algebras. Let $\alpha_t$ be the thermodynamic dynamics for the diagonal interaction of [[def-qsm-diagonal-ising-interaction]], as constructed under the exact hypotheses of [[thm-qsm-finite-range-spin-dynamics]]. For a local observable $A\in\mathcal A_X$, define the finite self-adjoint matrix
$$K_X:=\sum_{S:S\cap X\ne\varnothing}\Phi(S),$$
where the sum ranges over the singleton and pair supports of that Ising interaction. Then the sum is finite and
$$\alpha_t(A)=e^{itK_X/\hbar}Ae^{-itK_X/\hbar}\qquad(t\in\mathbb R).$$
In particular, every local diagonal observable is fixed by $\alpha_t$. The formula is exact for this commuting diagonal model and uses the full local matrix algebra; it does not restrict observables to diagonal matrices.

Assume Countable Choice and the finite-matrix C*-identity for the local spin algebras. Let $\omega$ be a $\beta$-KMS state, with $\beta>0$, for the thermodynamic dynamics of [[def-qsm-diagonal-ising-interaction]] in the full quasi-local matrix algebra. For every finite region $\Lambda$ and any two distinct product-basis configurations $\sigma,\tau\in\{-1,+1\}^\Lambda$, the local matrix unit $E_{\sigma,\tau}$ satisfies $\omega(E_{\sigma,\tau})=0$. Consequently the density matrix representing $\omega$ on each finite local matrix algebra is diagonal in the joint eigenbasis of the matrices $Z_i$.

Fix $d\geq1$, the inhomogeneous bounded finite-range diagonal spin-$\tfrac12$ Ising interaction of [[def-qsm-diagonal-ising-interaction]], $\beta>0$, $\hbar>0$, Countable Choice, and the finite-matrix C*-identity supplied by [[lem-qsm-finite-matrix-cstar-and-state-duality]]. Let $\mathcal A$ be its norm-completed quasi-local matrix algebra and let $\alpha_t$ be its thermodynamic dynamics. Let $\mathcal D_\beta$ be the set of Borel probability measures on $\{-1,+1\}^{\mathbb Z^d}$ fixed by every finite conditional kernel $\gamma_\Delta$ of the model. Let $\mathcal K_\beta$ be the set of $\beta$-KMS states for $\alpha$ on the full algebra $\mathcal A$, using the physical-time strip width $\beta\hbar$ seconds.

For a local matrix $A\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$, define its diagonal cylinder function by
$$\operatorname{diag}(A)(\sigma):=\langle A e_{\sigma|_\Lambda},e_{\sigma|_\Lambda}\rangle.$$
Then the map
$$\mathcal D_\beta\longrightarrow\mathcal K_\beta,\qquad \mu\longmapsto\omega_\mu,\qquad \omega_\mu(A):=\int\operatorname{diag}(A)(\sigma)\,d\mu(\sigma)\quad(A\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{loc}}),$$
extends uniquely to an affine bijection from classical DLR measures to $\beta$-KMS states. The KMS conclusion holds on the full matrix algebra, including off-diagonal observables; no translation invariance is assumed for this correspondence.

Assume Countable Choice, the finite-matrix C*-identity, $d=1$, finite $\beta>0$, $\hbar>0$, a uniform field $h_i=h\in\mathbb R$, and nearest-neighbor couplings $J_{i,i+1}=J_{i+1,i}=J\in\mathbb R$ with all other pair couplings zero, in the diagonal model of [[def-qsm-diagonal-ising-interaction]]. Then the full quasi-local matrix algebra has exactly one $\beta$-KMS state. The conclusion concerns the longitudinal diagonal Ising chain; no transverse-field term is included.

Assume Countable Choice, the finite-matrix C*-identity, $d\geq1$, a translation-invariant symmetric pair coupling $J_{i+k,j+k}=J_{ij}$ with $J_{ij}=0$ for $\|i-j\|_\infty>R$ for some finite $R$, a constant finite field $h_i=h\in\mathbb R$, and $\beta>0$, in the diagonal model of [[def-qsm-diagonal-ising-interaction]]. If
$$\sup_{i\in\mathbb Z^d}\sum_{j\ne i}\tanh(\beta|J_{ij}|)<1,$$
then the full quasi-local matrix algebra has exactly one $\beta$-KMS state. This strict influence bound is sufficient, not sharp. For homogeneous nearest-neighbor coupling $J$, it reduces to $2d\tanh(\beta|J|)<1$. The result is for the longitudinal diagonal interaction and makes no transverse-field claim.

Assume Countable Choice, the finite-matrix C*-identity, $d=2$, uniform nearest-neighbor coupling $J>0$, zero field, $\beta J\geq2$, and $\hbar>0$, in the diagonal spin-$\tfrac12$ model of [[def-qsm-diagonal-ising-interaction]]. Let $\tau_k$ be the spatial translation automorphisms of [[def-qsm-translation-invariant-spin-interaction]]; a state is **translation-invariant** when $\omega(\tau_k(A))=\omega(A)$ for every local $A$ and $k\in\mathbb Z^2$. Then there are two distinct translation-invariant full-algebra $\beta$-KMS states $\omega_+$ and $\omega_-$ with
$$\omega_+(Z_i)\geq m_*>0,\qquad \omega_-(Z_i)\leq-m_*<0\quad(i\in\mathbb Z^2),$$
where one may take $m_*=1-2\delta(\beta J)$, $\delta(K)=\frac43\,\frac{r^4(5-4r)}{(1-r)^2}$, and $r=3e^{-2K}$. This conservative bound does not assert extremality or that $\beta J=2$ is critical.

For the same uniform model with field parameter $h_i=h$, let
$$p_Q(h):=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{|\Lambda_n|}\log\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda_n}\!\left(e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda_n}(h)}\right),\qquad \Lambda_n=[-n,n]^2,$$
the dimensionless pressure per site along cubic boxes. This limit is the corresponding classical CSM pressure. It is not differentiable at $h=0$; for every $h>0$ its secant slope from zero is at least $\beta m_*$, and for every $h<0$ it is at most $-\beta m_*$. These are exact consequences of the stated diagonal model and the CSM suppliers, not empirical material claims.
For every bounded finite-range quantum spin model, uniqueness of the finite-volume Gibbs state for each finite region implies uniqueness of the infinite-volume KMS state.

transitive_in_run_suppliers.interface:
Fix an integer dimension $d\geq1$ and a finite nonempty alphabet $A$. A configuration is a function $\sigma:\mathbb Z^d\to A$. An interaction list consists of a finite index set $\mathcal R$ and, for each $r\in\mathcal R$, a finite nonempty shape $S_r\subset\mathbb Z^d$ containing $0$ and a function $\Phi_r:A^{S_r}\to\mathbb R$. The index $r$ is part of the data: two equal shapes with different indices represent two terms and are both counted. Every translate $x+S_r$ contributes once, with value $\Phi_r((\sigma_{x+y})_{y\in S_r})$.

The range is $R=\max_{r\in\mathcal R}\operatorname{diam}_\infty(S_r)$, with $R=0$ when $\mathcal R$ is empty. For finite $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d$, define the free-volume energy and the energy conditioned on an exterior configuration $\eta\in A^{\Lambda^c}$ by
$$H^{\mathrm{free}}_\Lambda(\sigma)=\sum_{r\in\mathcal R}\ \sum_{x:x+S_r\subseteq\Lambda}\Phi_r(\sigma_{x+S_r}),\qquad E_\Lambda(\tau_\Lambda\mid\eta)=\sum_{r\in\mathcal R}\ \sum_{x:(x+S_r)\cap\Lambda\ne\varnothing}\Phi_r((\tau_\Lambda\eta)_{x+S_r}).$$
These are finite sums: for each finite shape $S_r$, only finitely many anchors $x$ make $x+S_r$ meet $\Lambda$. Terms meeting $\Lambda$ but not contained in it appear in the conditional energy and not in the free-volume energy. The definitions are mathematical and assign no physical units; a physical model must state its units separately.

Assume Countable Choice for the product-measure extension framework of [[def-countable-choice]] and [[lem-csm-lattice-product-and-measure-compactness]]. Work in the finite-alphabet configuration space $X=A^{\mathbb Z^d}$ with its cylinder-generated Borel sigma-algebra. Let the finite-range interaction and its conditional energy be as in [[def-csm-finite-range-lattice-interaction]], and fix $\beta>0$. For a finite $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d$ and exterior configuration $\eta\in A^{\Lambda^c}$, put
$$Z_\Lambda^\eta=\sum_{\tau\in A^\Lambda}e^{-\beta E_\Lambda(\tau\mid\eta)},\qquad \gamma_\Lambda(f\mid\eta)=\frac{\sum_{\tau\in A^\Lambda}f(\tau\eta)e^{-\beta E_\Lambda(\tau\mid\eta)}}{Z_\Lambda^\eta}$$
for bounded measurable $f:X\to\mathbb R$. Here $\gamma_\Lambda f$ denotes the function $\eta\mapsto\gamma_\Lambda(f\mid\eta)$, composition is operator composition, and $\mu\gamma_\Lambda(f)=\int\gamma_\Lambda(f\mid\eta)\,d\mu(\eta)$. A proper kernel leaves every exterior-measurable event fixed. A specification is a family $(\gamma_\Lambda)_{\Lambda\text{ finite}}$ of proper probability kernels satisfying $\gamma_\Lambda\gamma_\Delta=\gamma_\Lambda$ whenever $\Delta\subseteq\Lambda$. A DLR state is a probability measure $\mu$ on $X$ satisfying $\mu\gamma_\Lambda=\mu$ for every finite $\Lambda$.

For the existence and uniqueness results below, a specification has **finite range** when for every finite $\Delta$ and every cylinder event $C$ the function $\eta\mapsto\gamma_\Delta(\mathbf1_C\mid\eta)$ depends on only finitely many coordinates of $\eta$. The displayed finite-range Gibbs formula has this property because only finitely many interaction terms meet $\Delta$, and a cylinder indicator depends on only finitely many additional coordinates.

The formula is the candidate Gibbs specification; [[lem-csm-lattice-specification-consistency]] establishes its positive finite normalization, measurability, properness and consistency under the stated hypotheses. The Countable Choice assumption is used for the product-measure construction, not for any finite conditional sum.

Assume Countable Choice. For finite $\beta>0$ and $J,h\in\mathbb R$, set $K=\beta J$, $b=\beta h$, and define the positive symmetric transfer matrix on $\{-1,+1\}$ by
$$T_{s,t}=e^{Kst+b(s+t)/2}.$$
Let $\lambda_+$ be its larger eigenvalue and let $r$ be its strictly positive unit eigenvector, with coordinates $r_s$. Then
$$Q_{s,t}=\frac{T_{s,t}r_t}{\lambda_+r_s},\qquad \pi_s=r_s^2$$
define a stochastic matrix $Q$ and invariant probability vector $\pi$. Their consistent consecutive-block laws $\pi_{s_\ell}\prod_{i=\ell}^{r-1}Q_{s_i,s_{i+1}}$ extend uniquely to a stationary probability measure on $\{-1,+1\}^{\mathbb Z}$.

Let $S$ be a finite nonempty set, $H:S\to\mathbb R$, and $\beta>0$. Define $Z=\sum_{s\in S}e^{-\beta H(s)}$ and $\gamma(s)=Z^{-1}e^{-\beta H(s)}$. For every probability vector $p$ on $S$, with $0\log0=0$, its Shannon entropy $H_{\rm Sh}(p)=-\sum_s p(s)\log p(s)$ and relative entropy $D(p\Vert\gamma)=\sum_{p(s)>0}p(s)\log(p(s)/\gamma(s))$ satisfy
$$D(p\Vert\gamma)=-H_{\rm Sh}(p)+\beta\sum_s p(s)H(s)+\log Z\geq0.$$
Equality holds exactly when $p=\gamma$. Equivalently, $\gamma$ is the unique minimizer of $\sum_s p(s)H(s)-\beta^{-1}H_{\rm Sh}(p)$, and the minimum is $-\beta^{-1}\log Z$.

For a finite-range Ising pair interaction on $\mathbb Z^d$ with spins $s_i\in\{-1,+1\}$, energy $-\sum_{\{i,j\}}J_{ij}s_is_j-\sum_i h_i s_i$, finite couplings, and $\beta>0$, let $\gamma_i(\cdot\mid\eta)$ be the one-site conditional Gibbs law. Define $c_{ij}$ as the supremum of the half-total-variation distance between $\gamma_i(\cdot\mid\eta)$ and $\gamma_i(\cdot\mid\eta')$ over boundaries differing only at $j$. Then $c_{ij}=0$ if no interaction term joins $i$ to $j$, and otherwise
$$c_{ij}\leq\tanh(\beta|J_{ij}|).$$
In particular, $\sup_i\sum_j\tanh(\beta|J_{ij}|)<1$ is a sufficient Dobrushin row-sum bound for every bounded field profile $(h_i)$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $d\geq1$, let $A$ be a finite nonempty set, and put $X=A^{\mathbb Z^d}$. Give $X$ the metric $d_X(\sigma,\eta)=\sum_{n\geq1}2^{-n}\mathbf 1_{\{\sigma_{i_n}\ne\eta_{i_n}\}}$ for a fixed enumeration $(i_n)$ of $\mathbb Z^d$, and let $\mathcal C$ be its cylinder algebra. Then $X$ is compact, the Borel sigma-algebra is $\sigma(\mathcal C)$, and every consistent normalized finitely additive probability on $\mathcal C$ extends uniquely to a probability on $\sigma(\mathcal C)$. Moreover, every sequence of probabilities on this sigma-algebra has a subsequence whose cylinder probabilities converge to those of a probability measure; along that subsequence integrals of every continuous $f:X\to\mathbb R$ converge.

Assume the finite-alphabet product-measure convention and conditional Gibbs formula of [[def-csm-lattice-gibbs-specification]], a finite-range interaction, and $\beta>0$. For every finite $\Lambda$ and exterior $\eta$, the displayed partition $Z_\Lambda^\eta$ is finite and strictly positive, the formula $\gamma_\Lambda(\cdot\mid\eta)$ defines a measurable proper probability kernel, and the family satisfies $\gamma_\Lambda\gamma_\Delta=\gamma_\Lambda$ whenever finite $\Delta\subseteq\Lambda$.

For probability vectors $p,q$ on a finite set $A$, there is a coupling $(X,Y)$ with $\Pr(X\ne Y)=\tfrac12\sum_{a\in A}|p(a)-q(a)|$. For a finite region $\Lambda$ with strictly positive single-site Gibbs conditionals, the random-scan heat-bath chain has the finite-volume Gibbs law as its unique stationary distribution. This chain is an auxiliary finite-state proof device, not a physical time evolution.

For the nearest-neighbor Ising model on a finite square box $B_n\subset\mathbb Z^2$ with exterior spins fixed to $+1$, coupling $J>0$, zero field, and $\beta>0$, let $\gamma_{B_n}^+$ be its normalized Gibbs law. For any simple dual cycle $\gamma$ that occurs in the disagreement graph of a configuration, let $A_\gamma$ be the event that all primal bonds crossed by $\gamma$ have disagreeing spins. Then
$$\gamma_{B_n}^+(A_\gamma)\leq e^{-2\beta J|\gamma|}.$$
For each such cycle, the parity-inside is defined by [[lem-csm-ising-parity-contours]] and lies in the variable box.

Assume Countable Choice, a translation-invariant finite-range interaction on $\mathbb Z^d$ with finite alphabet, and a nonempty DLR state set. Then there exists at least one translation-stationary DLR state. This assertion does not imply uniqueness or ergodicity.

Assume Countable Choice and let a consistent translation-stationary family of finite-dimensional distributions on a finite alphabet lattice be given. It extends to a unique stationary probability $\mu$ on the cylinder sigma-algebra. For any such stationary $\mu$ and any bounded translation-invariant finite-range interaction, define
$H_n=-\sum_{\sigma\in A^{B_n}}\mu_{B_n}(\sigma)\log\mu_{B_n}(\sigma)$ and
$u(\mu)=\sum_{r\in\mathcal R}\mathbb E_\mu[\Phi_r]$.
Then
$$h(\mu)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{H_n}{|B_n|}=\inf_{\ell\geq1}\frac{H_\ell}{|B_\ell|}$$
exists in $[0,\log|A|]$, and the free-boundary interaction-energy density satisfies
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\mathbb E_\mu[H^{\rm free}_{B_n}]}{|B_n|}=u(\mu).$$

Assume Countable Choice, finite $\beta>0$, finite $J,h\in\mathbb R$, and the one-dimensional nearest-neighbor Ising specification from [[def-csm-lattice-gibbs-specification]]. Then there is exactly one DLR state. It is the stationary Markov law constructed from the positive transfer matrix in [[lem-csm-chain-markov-bridge]]. For every fixed cylinder, finite-interval Gibbs probabilities converge to that law uniformly over the two endpoint boundary spins.

Assume Countable Choice, a finite-alphabet finite-range lattice specification on $\mathbb Z^d$, and $\beta>0$. For each pair of sites define $c_{ij}$ as the supremum of the half-total-variation change in the one-site conditional law at $i$ when only exterior spin $j$ is changed, with $c_{ii}=0$. If
$$c=\sup_i\sum_jc_{ij}<1,$$
then the DLR state is unique. Moreover, for a finite region $\Lambda$, two boundary conditions $\xi,\eta$, and a nonnegative integer $r$, if site $i$ has lattice $\ell^\infty$-distance at least $r(R+1)$ from $\Lambda^c$, its stationary disagreement probability in the finite-volume heat-bath coupling is at most $c^r/(1-c)$, where $R$ is the interaction range defined by [[def-csm-finite-range-lattice-interaction]]. Consequently every local conditional expectation becomes uniformly insensitive to boundary conditions as $\Lambda\uparrow\mathbb Z^d$.

Assume Countable Choice. For the two-dimensional nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic Ising model with $J>0$, $h=0$, and $\beta J\geq2$, the dimensionless pressure per site $p(h)$ as a function of field $h$ is not differentiable at $h=0$. More precisely, if the stationary DLR states at zero field have magnetizations at least $m_*>0$ and at most $-m_*$, then every positive-field secant slope from zero is at least $\beta m_*$ and every negative-field secant slope is at most $-\beta m_*$. This proves a sufficient coexistence cusp; it does not identify the critical coupling.

Assume Countable Choice, spins $s_i\in\{-1,+1\}$, inverse temperature $\beta>0$, a constant finite field $h\in\mathbb R$, and symmetric pair couplings satisfying $J_{ij}=J_{ji}$, $J_{i+k,j+k}=J_{ij}$ for all $i,j,k\in\mathbb Z^d$, and $J_{ij}=0$ when $\|i-j\|_\infty>R$ for some finite $R$. For finite $\Lambda$, use the conditional energy
$$E_\Lambda(s_\Lambda\mid\eta)=-\sum_{\{i,j\}:\{i,j\}\cap\Lambda\ne\varnothing}J_{ij}\widehat s_i\widehat s_j-h\sum_{i\in\Lambda}s_i,$$
where $\widehat s_i=s_i$ on $\Lambda$ and $\widehat s_i=\eta_i$ outside; let $\gamma$ be the corresponding finite-alphabet Gibbs specification from [[def-csm-lattice-gibbs-specification]]. If
$$\sup_i\sum_j\tanh(\beta|J_{ij}|)<1,$$
then there exists exactly one DLR state. For homogeneous nearest-neighbor coupling $J$ this sufficient condition is $2d\tanh(\beta|J|)<1$. It is not asserted to be sharp.

Assume Countable Choice. For the nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic Ising model on $\mathbb Z^2$ with coupling $J>0$, zero field, and $\beta J\geq2$, there exist two distinct translation-stationary DLR states $\mu_+$ and $\mu_-$ such that for every site $i$,
$$\mu_+(s_i)\geq m_*>0,\qquad \mu_-(s_i)\leq-m_*.$$
One may take $m_*=1-2\delta(\beta J)$, where
$$\delta(K)=\frac43\,\frac{r^4(5-4r)}{(1-r)^2},\qquad r=3e^{-2K}.$$
This is a sufficient low-temperature bound; the states are not asserted to be extremal and $K=2$ is not claimed to be critical.

Assume Countable Choice, a finite nonempty alphabet $A$, and a proper consistent finite-range specification $\gamma$ on $X=A^{\mathbb Z^d}$, with finite range as defined in [[def-csm-lattice-gibbs-specification]]. No translation invariance is required. For every exhaustion $\Lambda_n\uparrow\mathbb Z^d$ and every sequence of exterior configurations $\eta_n$, the measures $\gamma_{\Lambda_n}(\cdot\mid\eta_n)$ extended with the fixed exterior have a cylinder-convergent subsequence. Every such subsequential limit is a DLR state. Consequently the DLR state set is nonempty, convex, and closed under cylinder convergence. No uniqueness is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice, a bounded translation-invariant finite-range lattice interaction on a finite alphabet, and $\beta>0$. Let $p$ be its dimensionless pressure per site, and let $\mu$ be a translation-stationary probability with entropy density $h(\mu)$ and energy density $u(\mu)$ as in [[lem-csm-stationary-lattice-entropy-energy]]. Then
$$h(\mu)-\beta u(\mu)\leq p.$$
If $\mu$ is a DLR state for the specification, equality holds. Since stationary DLR states exist under these hypotheses, the supremum of $h(\mu)-\beta u(\mu)$ over stationary probabilities is attained and equals $p$. The converse “every maximizing stationary probability is DLR” is not asserted.

Let $d\geq1$, $A$ be finite nonempty, and let a bounded translation-invariant finite-range interaction on $A^{\mathbb Z^d}$ be as in [[def-csm-finite-range-lattice-interaction]]. Fix $\beta>0$. For a van Hove sequence of finite sets $\Lambda_n\subset\mathbb Z^d$, meaning $|\Lambda_n|\to\infty$ and $|\{x\in\Lambda_n:\operatorname{dist}_\infty(x,\Lambda_n^c)\leq r\}|/|\Lambda_n|\to0$ for every fixed $r$, the free-boundary pressure
$$p_{\Lambda_n}=\frac{1}{|\Lambda_n|}\log\sum_{\sigma\in A^{\Lambda_n}}e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda_n}^{\rm free}(\sigma)}$$
converges to the same finite limit as along cubic boxes. Bounded finite-range interactions are essential; this statement does not concern continuum particles or long-range models.

Let $H=H^*$ be a finite-dimensional Hamiltonian with energy unit J and let $\hbar>0$ have unit J s. For $t\in\mathbb R$, $U(t)=e^{-itH/\hbar}$ is unitary and $U(t+s)=U(t)U(s)$. For a density $\rho$, the Schrödinger state $U(t)\rho U(t)^*$ and the Heisenberg observable $\alpha_t(A)=U(t)^*AU(t)$ have the same trace expectation, and the von Neumann entropy is unchanged. If $\sigma_\beta=e^{-\beta H}/Z_\beta$, $Z_\beta=\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta H}$, then it is stationary and satisfies the finite Gibbs KMS strip identity
$
F_{A,B}(t+i\beta\hbar)=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_\beta\alpha_t(B)A),\qquad
F_{A,B}(z)=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_\beta A\alpha_z(B)),
$
where $\alpha_z(B)=e^{izH/\hbar}Be^{-izH/\hbar}$. The function is entire and bounded on $0\leq\operatorname{Im}z\leq\beta\hbar$. No infinite-volume KMS existence or approach to equilibrium follows.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, $D=\dim H\ge1$, with inner product linear in its first argument. With composition, Hilbert adjoint, identity and the induced operator norm, $\mathcal B(H)$ is a nonzero unital complex C*-algebra in the sense of [[def-c-star-algebra]]. In particular it is complete, $\|AB\|\le\|A\|\|B\|$, $\|A^*A\|=\|A\|^2$, $\|A^*\|=\|A\|$ and $\|I\|=1$. The matrix $\|A\|^2I-A^*A$ is positive semidefinite and has a positive square root in $\mathcal B(H)$.

Every complex-linear functional $\omega:\mathcal B(H)\to\mathbb C$ that is positive, meaning $\omega(B^*B)\ge0$ for all $B$, has a unique positive semidefinite matrix $\rho$ such that $\omega(A)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A)$ for all $A$. It is bounded and satisfies

$$|\omega(A)|\le\operatorname{Tr}(\rho)\|A\|\quad(A\in\mathcal B(H)),\qquad \|\omega\|=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho)=\omega(I).$$

Consequently the canonical states of [[def-state-on-a-c-star-algebra]] are exactly the trace pairings of density operators of [[def-qc-density-operator]]; for a positive functional, normalization $\omega(I)=1$ is equivalent to norm one. The result includes zero positive functionals, nonfaithful densities and $D=1$; it makes no infinite-dimensional density representation assertion.

Let $H$ be a complex inner-product space of finite dimension $D\geq1$, with inner product linear in its first argument. Every Hermitian endomorphism $M$ has an orthonormal eigenbasis with real eigenvalues. For a real function $f$ on its finite spectrum, define $f(M)$ by its spectral projections; this definition is independent of the choice of eigenbasis. In particular positive square roots, exponentials, and logarithms on positive supports are well defined.

For a density matrix $\rho$ on $H$, meaning a Hermitian positive semidefinite operator with $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$, $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A)=\sum_jp_j\langle Au_j,u_j\rangle$ for bounded $A$, where $\rho=\sum_jp_j|u_j\rangle\langle u_j|$. The weighted form $(X,Y)_\rho=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho X^*Y)$ satisfies Cauchy–Schwarz, $|(X,Y)_\rho|^2\leq(X,X)_\rho(Y,Y)_\rho$. Finally, $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho^2)\leq1$, with equality exactly for rank-one densities, and those are exactly the extreme points of the finite density-matrix set.

Let $\mathcal A$ be the unital quasi-local spin C*-algebra of [[def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra]], whose C*-structure uses Countable Choice as in [[lem-qsm-quasilocal-completion]]. An **infinite algebraic state** is a bounded complex-linear functional $\omega:\mathcal A\to\mathbb C$ satisfying $\omega(I)=1$ and $\omega(A^*A)\ge0$ for every $A\in\mathcal A$.

For each finite region $\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb Z^d$, the restriction $\omega|_{\mathcal A_\Lambda}$ is a finite-matrix state. By [[lem-qsm-finite-matrix-cstar-and-state-duality]], every positive normalized functional on a finite matrix algebra is represented by a unique density matrix. Define its **local density matrix** $\rho_\Lambda$ by

$$\omega(A)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda}(\rho_\Lambda A)\qquad(A\in\mathcal A_\Lambda),$$

where $\rho_\Lambda=\rho_\Lambda^*\ge0$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda}\rho_\Lambda=1$. For $\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda'$, the local densities are **consistent** when $\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}(\rho_{\Lambda'})=\rho_\Lambda$, with partial trace characterized by its pairing against every $A\otimes I_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}$. No density operator on a globally chosen Hilbert space is part of this definition.

This agrees with the canonical state convention of [[def-state-on-a-c-star-algebra]]: the finite restrictions have norm one by [[lem-qsm-finite-matrix-cstar-and-state-duality]], giving $|\omega(A)|\le\|A\|$ on the dense local algebra and hence on its completion; evaluation at the norm-one identity gives $\|\omega\|=1$. Conversely a canonical state has local restrictions with density matrices of trace one, since the finite norm formula and continuity on the dense local algebra imply $\|\omega\|=\omega(I)$. No global density representation is asserted.

Fix an integer dimension $d\ge1$, the countable site set $\Gamma=\mathbb{Z}^d$ of [[lem-qsm-integer-lattice-countable]], and one finite spin dimension $q\ge1$. Equip $\Gamma$ with the max-coordinate metric $d_\infty(x,y)=\max_{1\le r\le d}|x_r-y_r|$; symmetry and separation hold coordinatewise, and the triangle inequality follows from $|x_r-z_r|\le|x_r-y_r|+|y_r-z_r|$ for every coordinate. A **finite region** is a finite subset $\Lambda\subseteq\Gamma$; its cardinality is $|\Lambda|$.

For a finite region $\Lambda$, let $S_\Lambda=\{1,\ldots,q\}^{\Lambda}$ be the set of spin configurations on $\Lambda$ and let $\mathcal H_\Lambda$ be the vector space of functions $f:S_\Lambda\to\mathbb C$ with inner product $\langle f,g\rangle=\sum_{s\in S_\Lambda}f(s)\overline{g(s)}$. For each $s\in S_\Lambda$, let $e_s$ be the indicator function of $\{s\}$; these vectors form an orthonormal basis. For $\Lambda=\varnothing$, $S_\Lambda$ is a singleton and $\mathcal H_\Lambda\cong\mathbb C$. The **local spin matrix algebra** is

$$\mathcal A_\Lambda:=\mathcal B(\mathcal H_\Lambda)\cong M_{q^{|\Lambda|}}(\mathbb C),$$

Here $\mathcal B(\mathcal H_\Lambda)$ denotes all complex-linear endomorphisms of the finite-dimensional Hilbert space; they are bounded. The algebra has composition, Hilbert adjoint, identity $I_\Lambda$, and induced operator norm

$$\|T\|:=\sup_{\|\xi\|=1}\|T\xi\|.$$

The **finite local trace** is $\operatorname{Tr}_\Lambda(T):=\sum_{s\in S_\Lambda}\langle T e_s,e_s\rangle$ in the displayed configuration basis $(e_s)$. This is the usual finite-matrix trace; basis independence and its cyclic/unitary identities are supplied by [[lem-qsm-matrix-state-calculus]].

If $\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda'$, restriction of configurations gives the canonical factorization $\mathcal H_{\Lambda'}\cong\mathcal H_\Lambda\otimes\mathcal H_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}$, with sites ordered lexicographically. The **factor inclusion** is the unital $*$-homomorphism $\iota_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}:\mathcal A_\Lambda\to\mathcal A_{\Lambda'}$ given by $T\mapsto T\otimes I_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}$. A **localization region** for $T$ is any finite $\Lambda$ for which $T\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$ under these inclusions; a localization region need not be minimal.

The ordinary operator norm makes each local matrix algebra a nonzero unital complete C*-algebra, and every positive normalized complex-linear functional is uniquely a trace pairing with a density matrix, by [[lem-qsm-finite-matrix-cstar-and-state-duality]]. This includes the empty region, whose Hilbert space is $\mathbb C$. This definition does not posit an infinite-dimensional tensor-product Hilbert space.

Use the finite local matrix algebras and isometric factor inclusions of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]] and [[lem-qsm-local-spin-inclusions-isometric]]. Identify $A\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$ with its image in every larger finite-region algebra. The directed union

$$\mathcal A_{\mathrm{loc}}:=\bigcup_{\Lambda\subseteq\Gamma,\ |\Lambda|<\infty}\mathcal A_\Lambda$$

is the algebra of **strictly local observables**. Its norm is $\|A\|=\|A\|_{\mathcal A_\Lambda}$ for any finite localization region $\Lambda$ of $A$; isometric inclusions make this independent of the chosen region. The **quasi-local spin algebra** is the norm completion

$$\mathcal A:=\overline{\mathcal A_{\mathrm{loc}}}^{\,\|\cdot\|}.$$

The C*-algebra structure on this completion has product and adjoint extended continuously from the finite local matrix algebras. Countable Choice is assumed for the published existence theorem for metric completions; [[lem-qsm-quasilocal-completion]] supplies the full extension argument using the finite C*-identity of [[lem-qsm-finite-matrix-cstar-and-state-duality]].

**No global Hilbert tensor product is selected.** “Quasi-local” means norm completion of the directed algebra of finite-region observables; it does not mean a chosen representation as operators on an infinite tensor-product Hilbert space. A local operator $A\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$ may have more than one localization region. Disjoint finite local factors commute in their common finite tensor algebra.
For every positive integer $d$, the integer lattice $\Gamma=\mathbb{Z}^d$ is at most countable. Countability here means finite or in bijection with $\mathbb{N}$, as in [[def-countable]].

Fix $d\ge1$, $q\ge1$, and finite regions $\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda'\subseteq\mathbb Z^d$ as in [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]]. Then the factor inclusion $\iota_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}(T)=T\otimes I$ is an isometric unital $*$-homomorphism:

$$\|\iota_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}(T)\|=\|T\|\qquad(T\in\mathcal A_\Lambda).$$

For nested finite regions $\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda'\subseteq\Lambda''$, the inclusions compose: $\iota_{\Lambda',\Lambda''}\circ\iota_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}=\iota_{\Lambda,\Lambda''}$.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the Cauchy-sequence completion. For the local spin system of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]], the normed $*$-algebra $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{loc}}$ and its completion $\mathcal A$ of [[def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra]] are well defined; $\mathcal A$ is a unital complex C*-algebra and $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{loc}}$ is norm dense in it. If $A\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$ and $B\in\mathcal A_\Delta$ for disjoint finite regions $\Lambda,\Delta$, then $AB=BA$.

Use the lattice $\Gamma=\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge1$, the finite spin dimension $q\ge1$, the local matrix algebras $\mathcal A_\Lambda$, and the max-coordinate metric $d_\infty$ of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]]. For finite nonempty $Z\subset\Gamma$, write $\operatorname{diam}_\infty Z=\max_{x,y\in Z}d_\infty(x,y)$; for finite nonempty $X,Y\subset\Gamma$, write $\operatorname{dist}_\infty(X,Y)=\min_{x\in X,y\in Y}d_\infty(x,y)$.

A **uniformly bounded finite-range interaction** is a family $\Phi(Z)\in\mathcal A_Z$, indexed by finite nonempty $Z\subset\Gamma$, such that $\Phi(Z)^*=\Phi(Z)$ and there are an integer $M\ge1$, a finite $R\ge0$, and $\kappa<\infty$ satisfying

$$\Phi(Z)=0\quad\text{if }|Z|>M\text{ or }\operatorname{diam}_\infty Z>R,\qquad\kappa:=\sup_{x\in\Gamma}\sum_{Z\ni x}\|\Phi(Z)\|<\infty.$$

The norm in this sum is the operator norm in the local matrix algebra $\mathcal A_Z$. If a model lists several terms with the same support, first add them in that local algebra; the resulting single operator is $\Phi(Z)$, and $\kappa$ uses its norm. Thus no multiplicity is implicit.

For a finite region $\Lambda\subset\Gamma$, define the **free-boundary finite-volume Hamiltonian** by summing only terms whose complete support lies inside $\Lambda$; terms meeting $\Lambda$ but extending outside it are omitted:

$$H_\Lambda:=\sum_{\varnothing\ne Z\subseteq\Lambda}\Phi(Z)\in\mathcal A_\Lambda.$$

It is a finite sum of self-adjoint matrices. For a fixed scale $\hbar>0$ and any finite $\Omega\supseteq\Lambda$, embed $H_\Lambda$ in $\mathcal A_\Omega$ by the canonical factor inclusion and define

$$\alpha_t^\Lambda(A):=e^{itH_\Lambda/\hbar}Ae^{-itH_\Lambda/\hbar}\qquad(A\in\mathcal A_\Omega,\ t\in\mathbb R).$$

These actions are compatible as $\Omega$ increases, because the extra tensor factors carry the identity. On $\mathcal A_\Lambda$ this is the ordinary finite matrix Heisenberg dynamics.

In physical SI bookkeeping, when $\Phi(Z)$ is interpreted as an energy, $\Phi(Z)$, $\kappa$, and $H_\Lambda$ have units J, $t$ has units s, and $\hbar$ is the adopted reduced Planck constant with units J s. The mathematics below uses only $\hbar>0$ and asserts no measured parameter value.

Let $\Phi$ be an interaction of [[def-qsm-bounded-finite-range-interaction]], fix $\mu>0$, and let $X\subseteq\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda'$ be finite regions with $X\ne\varnothing$. For every $A\in\mathcal A_X$ and $t\in\mathbb R$,

$$\|\alpha_t^{\Lambda'}(A)-\alpha_t^\Lambda(A)\|\le\frac{2\kappa |X|\|A\||t|}{\hbar}e^{(2\kappa M e^{\mu R}/\hbar)|t|+\mu R}\sum_{y\notin\Lambda}e^{-\mu\operatorname{dist}_\infty(X,\{y\})}.$$

The infinite sum is finite. It tends to zero as $\Lambda$ exhausts $\mathbb Z^d$, so the estimate gives compact-time norm Cauchy convergence of free-boundary finite-volume dynamics on each local observable.

Let $\Phi$ be an interaction of [[def-qsm-bounded-finite-range-interaction]] with parameters $M,R,\kappa,\hbar$. Let $\mu>0$, let $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d$ be finite, let $X\subseteq\Lambda$ be finite and nonempty, and let $Y\subset\mathbb Z^d$ be any finite nonempty set. Take $A\in\mathcal A_X$ and $B\in\mathcal A_Y$, with both embedded in the common finite algebra $\mathcal A_{\Lambda\cup Y}$. Then for every $t\in\mathbb R$,

$$\bigl\|[\alpha_t^\Lambda(A),B]\bigr\|\le 2\|A\|\,\|B\|\,|X|\exp\!\left(\frac{2\kappa M e^{\mu R}}{\hbar}|t|-\mu\operatorname{dist}_\infty(X,Y)\right).$$

Here the finite-volume dynamics is extended by the identity on sites outside $\Lambda$, as in [[def-qsm-bounded-finite-range-interaction]]. The parameter $\mu$ is measured per lattice step in the dimensionless max-coordinate metric. The bound is uniform over finite volumes containing $X$; it is an operator-norm estimate for the stipulated spin model, not a relativistic light cone.

Assume Countable Choice and the finite-matrix C*-identity condition [A1] below. Let $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{loc}}=\bigcup_{\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d,\ |\Lambda|<\infty}\mathcal A_\Lambda$ and let $\mathcal A$ be its norm completion as in [[def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra]]. These assumptions give the conditional unital C*-algebra structure supplied by [[lem-qsm-quasilocal-completion]]. Let $\Phi$ be a uniformly bounded finite-range interaction of [[def-qsm-bounded-finite-range-interaction]].

For any increasing finite exhaustion $\Lambda_n\uparrow\mathbb Z^d$, the free-boundary finite-volume maps $\alpha_t^{\Lambda_n}$ converge in norm on every local observable, uniformly for $t$ in compact intervals. Their limit is independent of the exhaustion and extends uniquely to a strongly continuous one-parameter group $\alpha_t$ of $*$-automorphisms of $\mathcal A$. Strong continuity means $t\mapsto\alpha_t(A)$ is norm-continuous for every fixed $A\in\mathcal A$. This result does not assert that an infinite-volume Hamiltonian is an element of $\mathcal A$ or a bounded operator on a preselected infinite tensor-product Hilbert space.

Use the lattice $\Gamma=\mathbb Z^d$, the finite-site Hilbert spaces, local matrix algebras, factor inclusions, and norm-completed local algebra $\mathcal A$ of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]] and [[def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra]]. Write $\tau_x$ for spatial translation by $x\in\Gamma$. For a finite region $\Lambda$ and its configuration basis $(e_s)_{s\in\{1,\ldots,q\}^{\Lambda}}$, the bijection $s\mapsto s_x$ defined by $s_x(y+x)=s(y)$ gives a unitary $U_{x,\Lambda}:\mathcal H_\Lambda\to\mathcal H_{\Lambda+x}$ by $U_{x,\Lambda}e_s=e_{s_x}$. On $A\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$ put $\tau_x(A)=U_{x,\Lambda}AU_{x,\Lambda}^*$.

For $x,y\in\Gamma$, the basis relabellings satisfy $U_{x,\Lambda+y}U_{y,\Lambda}=U_{x+y,\Lambda}$, since both sides send each configuration vector $e_s$ to $e_{s_{x+y}}$. Consequently $\tau_0$ is the identity and $\tau_{x+y}=\tau_x\circ\tau_y$ on local observables; continuity extends the action law to $\mathcal A$.

This local map is independent of the chosen localization region: enlarging $\Lambda$ tensors both representatives with identities, and the same site relabelling gives the corresponding enlarged unitary. On each finite region it is a unitary conjugation, hence isometric and preserves products, adjoints, and identities. It therefore extends uniquely to an isometric *-automorphism of the norm completion $\mathcal A$: if $A_n$ is local and converges to $A$, define $\tau_x(A)=\lim_n\tau_x(A_n)$; isometry makes this limit independent of the approximating sequence, and $\tau_{-x}$ is its inverse. This construction uses the norm-completion property and the isometric local maps; it does not use the separate finite-matrix C*-identity condition.

Let $\Phi$ be a uniformly bounded finite-range interaction in the sense of [[def-qsm-bounded-finite-range-interaction]], with parameters $M,R,\kappa$. It is translation invariant when $\tau_x(\Phi(Z))=\Phi(Z+x)$ for every finite nonempty support $Z$ and every $x\in\Gamma$. Let $\mathscr S_\Phi$ contain one representative of each nonzero translation orbit, anchored so that the lexicographically least site of each representative is $0$, using the standard coordinate lexicographic order on $\mathbb Z^d$. The least site exists because each support is finite and nonempty; every representative contains $0$. The list $\mathscr S_\Phi$ is finite: every such support has at most $M$ sites and lies in the finite cube $[-\lceil R\rceil,\lceil R\rceil]^d$. For finite $\Lambda$, the free-boundary Hamiltonian is $H_\Lambda=\sum_{Z\subseteq\Lambda}\Phi(Z)$, as in the interaction definition.

When $\Phi(Z)$ represents an energy, its norm, $H_\Lambda$, and the constant $J_\Phi:=\sum_{S\in\mathscr S_\Phi}\|\Phi(S)\|$ have units joules. The definition is mathematical and makes no empirical identification of an interaction with a material.

Here a complex C$^*$-algebra is a complex Banach algebra with associative bilinear multiplication, submultiplicative norm, and a conjugate-linear involution satisfying $\|A^*A\|=\|A\|^2$; **unital** means that it has a nonzero identity $I$ ([[def-c-star-algebra]]). A $*$-automorphism is a bijective complex-linear map preserving multiplication and involution. Let $t\mapsto\alpha_t$ be a one-parameter group of such automorphisms, so $\alpha_0$ is the identity and $\alpha_s\alpha_t=\alpha_{s+t}$. It is **strongly continuous** when $t\mapsto\alpha_t(A)$ is norm-continuous for each fixed $A\in\mathcal A$. A **state** is a bounded complex-linear functional $\omega:\mathcal A\to\mathbb C$ with $\omega(I)=1$ and $\omega(A^*A)\ge0$ for every $A\in\mathcal A$; this is the state convention of [[def-qsm-infinite-algebraic-state]].

Fix absolute temperature $T>0$ in kelvins and Boltzmann's constant $k_B>0$ in J K$^{-1}$; the inverse-temperature parameter is $\beta:=(k_BT)^{-1}>0$, measured in J$^{-1}$. Let the reduced Planck constant $\hbar>0$ have units J s. Write $b:=\beta\hbar$, measured in seconds, and

$$S_b:=\{z\in\mathbb C:0\le\operatorname{Im}z\le b\},\qquad S_b^\circ:=\{z\in\mathbb C:0<\operatorname{Im}z<b\}.$$

A state $\omega$ is a **$\beta$-KMS state for $\alpha$ in physical time** when for every $A,B\in\mathcal A$ there is a bounded function $F_{A,B}:S_b\to\mathbb C$ (that is, $\sup_{z\in S_b}|F_{A,B}(z)|<\infty$) that is continuous on $S_b$, complex-differentiable at every point of $S_b^\circ$, and satisfies

$$F_{A,B}(t)=\omega\!\left(A\alpha_t(B)\right),\qquad F_{A,B}(t+ib)=\omega\!\left(\alpha_t(B)A\right)\quad(t\in\mathbb R).$$

For the assigned quantum spin model, $\mathcal A$ is the norm-completed quasi-local algebra of [[def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra]] and $\alpha$ is the thermodynamic dynamics of [[thm-qsm-finite-range-spin-dynamics]], under that theorem's stated hypotheses. The strip width is $\beta\hbar$ in physical seconds; setting $\hbar=1$ is a separate natural-unit convention. This is a mathematical equilibrium criterion for the specified algebra and dynamics. It does not assert that a model describes a material, that a system has dynamically relaxed, or that all stationary states are KMS.

Let $b>0$ and $S_b=\{z\in\mathbb C:0\le\operatorname{Im}z\le b\}$, with interior $S_b^\circ=\{z:0<\operatorname{Im}z<b\}$. Let $F:S_b\to\mathbb C$ be bounded (so $\sup_{z\in S_b}|F(z)|<\infty$), continuous, and complex-differentiable at every point of $S_b^\circ$, and set

$$M_0:=\sup_{t\in\mathbb R}|F(t)|,\qquad M_1:=\sup_{t\in\mathbb R}|F(t+ib)|.$$

For $0<s<b$,

$$\sup_{t\in\mathbb R}|F(t+is)|\le M_0^{1-s/b}M_1^{s/b},$$

where each exponent is positive and $0^r=0$ for $r>0$. In particular, if $M_0,M_1\le C$ then $|F(z)|\le C$ on $S_b$. If two bounded continuous functions on $S_b$, holomorphic inside, have the same lower boundary values, then they agree on all of $S_b$.

Let $\mathcal H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space, let $H=H^*$ on $\mathcal H$ with energy units J, let $\hbar>0$ have units J s, and let $\beta>0$ have units J$^{-1}$. Write $\operatorname{Tr}$ for the ordinary finite-dimensional trace. Assume the finite spectral-calculus and unital C$^*$-algebra clauses [A1]–[A2] below. Define the finite-matrix Heisenberg group

$$\alpha_t^H(X):=e^{itH/\hbar}Xe^{-itH/\hbar}\qquad(X\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H),\ t\in\mathbb R).$$

A state $\omega$ on the unital C$^*$-algebra $\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ satisfies the $\beta$-KMS strip condition of [[def-qsm-kms-state]] for $\alpha^H$ if and only if

$$\omega(X)=\frac{\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H}X)}{\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H})}\qquad(X\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)).$$

Here $\beta$ has units J$^{-1}$, $H$ has units J, and the physical-time strip has width $\beta\hbar$ seconds. The result is finite-dimensional and makes no infinite-volume or relaxation claim.

Definition

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Statement

Let $\mathcal P$ be a pi-system on $X$. Then
$\lambda_X(\mathcal P)=\sigma_X(\mathcal P)$. Consequently, if $\mathcal D$ is

Statement

Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb C$ be open, let each $f_n:\Omega\to\mathbb C$ be holomorphic, and suppose $f_n\to f$ locally uniformly on $\Omega$. Then $f$ is holomorphic and

$$f_n^{(k)}\longrightarrow f^{(k)}$$

locally uniformly on $\Omega$ for every natural $k$, with $f^{(0)}=f$.

A locally uniform limit of holomorphic functions is holomorphic, and for every natural $k$ the $k$th derivatives converge locally uniformly to the $k$th derivative of the limit.

direct_item_inputs.interface_excerpt: Use the lattice $\Gamma=\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge1$, the finite spin dimension $q\ge1$, the local matrix algebras $\mathcal A_\Lambda$, and the max-coordinate metric $d_\infty$ of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]]. For finite nonempty $Z\subset\Gamma$, write $\operatorname{diam}_\infty Z=\max_{x,y\in Z}d_\infty(x,y)$; for finite nonempty $X,Y\subset\Gamma$, write $\operatorname{dist}_\infty(X,Y)=\min_{x\in X,y\in Y}d_\infty(x,y)$. A **uniformly bounded finite-range interaction** is a family $\Phi(Z)\in\mathcal A_Z$, indexed by finite nonempty $Z\subset\Gamma$, such that $\Phi(Z)^*=\Phi(Z)$ and there are an integer $M\ge1$, a finite $R\ge0$, and $\kappa<\infty$ satisfying $$\Phi(Z)=0\quad\text{if }|Z|>M\text{ or }\operatorname{diam}_\infty Z>R,\qquad\kappa:=\sup_{x\in\Gamma}\sum_{Z\ni x}\|\Phi(Z)\|<\infty.$$ The norm in this sum is the operator norm in the local matrix algebra $\mathcal A_Z$. If a model lists several terms with the same support, first add them in that local algebra; the resulting single operator is $\Phi(Z)$, and $\kappa$ uses its norm. Thus no multiplicity is implicit. For a finite region $\Lambda\subset\Gamma$, define the **free-boundary finite-volume Hamiltonian** by summing only terms whose complete support lies inside $\Lambda$; terms meeting $\Lambda$ but extending outside it are omitted: $$H_\Lambda:=\sum_{\varnothing\ne Z\subseteq\Lambda}\Phi(Z)\in\mathcal A_\Lambda.$$ It is a finite sum of self-adjoint matrices. For a fixed scale $\hbar>0$ and any finite $\Omega\supseteq\Lambda$, embed $H_\Lambda$ in $\mathcal A_\Omega$ by the canonical factor inclusion and define $$\alpha_t^\Lambda(A):=e^{itH_\Lambda/\hbar}Ae^{-itH_\Lambda/\hbar}\qquad(A\in\mathcal A_\Omega,\ t\in\mathbb R).$$ These actions are compatible as $\Omega$ increases, because the extra tensor factors carry the identity. On $\mathcal A_\Lambda$ this is the ordinary finite matrix Heisenberg dynamics. In physical SI bookkeeping, when $\Phi(Z)$ is interpreted as an energy, $\Phi(Z)$, $\kappa$, and $H_\Lambda$ have units J, $t$ has units s, and $\hbar$ is the adopted reduced Planck constant with units J s. The mathematics below uses only $\hbar>0$ and asserts no measured parameter value.

Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a separable complex Hilbert space, with inner product linear in its first argument. An operator $\rho\in\mathcal B(H)$ is a **density operator** when it is positive, trace class, and $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$. Here trace class means compact with summable singular values, and $\operatorname{Tr}$ is the basis-independent trace of a trace-class operator. The **normal density state represented by $\rho$** is the functional on bounded operators $ \omega_\rho(A):=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A),\qquad A\in\mathcal B(H). $ In this page, “normal density state” means this specified trace-pairing representation; no equivalence with other definitions of normal functionals is assumed. The trace pairing is used only for bounded $A$. Unbounded observables are treated through their spectral probability measures in [[lem-qsm-trace-state-calculus]].

Here a complex C$^*$-algebra is a complex Banach algebra with associative bilinear multiplication, submultiplicative norm, and a conjugate-linear involution satisfying $\|A^*A\|=\|A\|^2$; **unital** means that it has a nonzero identity $I$ ([[def-c-star-algebra]]). A $*$-automorphism is a bijective complex-linear map preserving multiplication and involution. Let $t\mapsto\alpha_t$ be a one-parameter group of such automorphisms, so $\alpha_0$ is the identity and $\alpha_s\alpha_t=\alpha_{s+t}$. It is **strongly continuous** when $t\mapsto\alpha_t(A)$ is norm-continuous for each fixed $A\in\mathcal A$. A **state** is a bounded complex-linear functional $\omega:\mathcal A\to\mathbb C$ with $\omega(I)=1$ and $\omega(A^*A)\ge0$ for every $A\in\mathcal A$; this is the state convention of [[def-qsm-infinite-algebraic-state]]. Fix absolute temperature $T>0$ in kelvins and Boltzmann's constant $k_B>0$ in J K$^{-1}$; the inverse-temperature parameter is $\beta:=(k_BT)^{-1}>0$, measured in J$^{-1}$. Let the reduced Planck constant $\hbar>0$ have units J s. Write $b:=\beta\hbar$, measured in seconds, and $$S_b:=\{z\in\mathbb C:0\le\operatorname{Im}z\le b\},\qquad S_b^\circ:=\{z\in\mathbb C:0<\operatorname{Im}z<b\}.$$ A state $\omega$ is a **$\beta$-KMS state for $\alpha$ in physical time** when for every $A,B\in\mathcal A$ there is a bounded function $F_{A,B}:S_b\to\mathbb C$ (that is, $\sup_{z\in S_b}|F_{A,B}(z)|<\infty$) that is continuous on $S_b$, complex-differentiable at every point of $S_b^\circ$, and satisfies $$F_{A,B}(t)=\omega\!\left(A\alpha_t(B)\right),\qquad F_{A,B}(t+ib)=\omega\!\left(\alpha_t(B)A\right)\quad(t\in\mathbb R).$$ For the assigned quantum spin model, $\mathcal A$ is the norm-completed quasi-local algebra of [[def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra]] and $\alpha$ is the thermodynamic dynamics of [[thm-qsm-finite-range-spin-dynamics]], under that theorem's stated hypotheses. The strip width is $\beta\hbar$ in physical seconds; setting $\hbar=1$ is a separate natural-unit convention. This is a mathematical equilibrium criterion for the specified algebra and dynamics. It does not assert that a model describes a material, that a system has dynamically relaxed, or that all stationary states are KMS.

Fix an integer dimension $d\ge1$, the countable site set $\Gamma=\mathbb{Z}^d$ of [[lem-qsm-integer-lattice-countable]], and one finite spin dimension $q\ge1$. Equip $\Gamma$ with the max-coordinate metric $d_\infty(x,y)=\max_{1\le r\le d}|x_r-y_r|$; symmetry and separation hold coordinatewise, and the triangle inequality follows from $|x_r-z_r|\le|x_r-y_r|+|y_r-z_r|$ for every coordinate. A **finite region** is a finite subset $\Lambda\subseteq\Gamma$; its cardinality is $|\Lambda|$. For a finite region $\Lambda$, let $S_\Lambda=\{1,\ldots,q\}^{\Lambda}$ be the set of spin configurations on $\Lambda$ and let $\mathcal H_\Lambda$ be the vector space of functions $f:S_\Lambda\to\mathbb C$ with inner product $\langle f,g\rangle=\sum_{s\in S_\Lambda}f(s)\overline{g(s)}$. For each $s\in S_\Lambda$, let $e_s$ be the indicator function of $\{s\}$; these vectors form an orthonormal basis.
